$comment: ★★★ UCRT-P5 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION) — `library.pe` IS NOW ucrtbase.dll, AND THE TF-C111 SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE WAS WRONG IN ITS CONCLUSION, NOT IN ITS MEASUREMENT. It read: 'FORCED: ucrtbase.dll exports NO `_setjmp` at all … the UCRT moved setjmp into the static vcruntime lib, so there is no ucrtbase name to bind'. The first clause is TRUE and still is; the inference drawn from it is FALSE, and it froze this descriptor on the legacy CRT for two phases. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-11 (`objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, GNU binutils 2.42): ucrtbase exports the setjmp facility under FOUR names — `__intrinsic_setjmp` (ordinal 75, RVA 0xed430), `__intrinsic_setjmpex` (ord 76, 0xed4f0), the unprefixed `setjmp` (ord 2371, 0xed4d0) and `longjmp` (ord 2290, 0xb30f0). WHAT IS ABSENT IS THE SPELLING `_setjmp`, NOT THE FUNCTION. Looking up one name, finding nothing, and concluding the facility was gone is precisely the error this paragraph now exists to prevent. ★ THE BIND IS ABI-IDENTICAL, PROVEN BY DISASSEMBLY RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `ucrtbase.__intrinsic_setjmp`@0xed430 is INSTRUCTION-FOR-INSTRUCTION the same code as `msvcrt._setjmp`@0x7ab10 — `mov [rcx],rdx` (the SECOND argument, the frame, into `_JUMP_BUFFER.Frame`@0), then rbx@8, rsp@0x10 (`lea r8,[rsp+8]`), rbp@0x18, rsi@0x20, rdi@0x28, r12-r15@0x30-0x48, rip@0x50, `stmxcsr`@0x58, `fnstcw`@0x5c, `movdqa` xmm6-xmm15@0x60-0xf0, `xor eax,eax; ret`. SAME 2-arg (env, frame) contract, SAME 256B/16-aligned buffer this file already declares, SAME `movdqa` alignment requirement — so nothing below this line had to change. (`ucrtbase.setjmp`@0xed4d0 is a bare `jmp 0xed430` tail-thunk to it — NOT a 1-arg wrapper that synthesizes a frame; it forwards whatever RDX holds, which is why it would have been an equally correct bind.) `ucrtbase.longjmp`@0xb30f0 matches `msvcrt.longjmp`@0x33690 byte-for-byte too, modulo the two relative displacements. ★ WHY `__intrinsic_setjmp` AND NOT THE UNPREFIXED `setjmp`: because the authoring rule D-FFI-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-LINK-NAME already states the test — 'does a real compiler for THIS target emit THIS name for THIS C identifier' — and ✔MEASURED, it does. MSVC's own x64 import library `vcruntime.lib` contains `__imp___intrinsic_setjmp` + `__intrinsic_setjmp` and NO `_setjmp` and NO bare `setjmp`: `<setjmp.h>` does `#define setjmp _setjmp` (MSVC 14.51 setjmp.h:130) and the COMPILER INTRINSIC lowers `_setjmp` into a call to `__intrinsic_setjmp`. The SDK's `ucrt.lib` carries no setjmp symbol at all (instrument validated with a positive control: the same sweep finds `memcpy_s` and 44 `printf` rows). `vcruntime140.dll` likewise exports `__intrinsic_setjmp`/`__intrinsic_setjmpex`/`longjmp` but no bare `setjmp`, so `__intrinsic_setjmp` is the ONE name common to the whole modern MSVC runtime family, while bare `setjmp` is a ucrtbase-only convenience. The api-set `api-ms-win-crt-private-l1-1-0.dll` forwards all four names to `ucrtbase.*`, which is the OS's own statement of where they live. ⇒ the DSS-VISIBLE identifier stays `_setjmp` (MSVC's `<setjmp.h>` vocabulary, so C source that spells `_setjmp` keeps compiling) and `linkName` moves ONLY the external name — a flat string, not a `when:{format:pe}` variant, because the row's `availableObjectFormats:["pe"]` already owns that fact and restating it would create a second owner. ★ THE CO-STATE ARGUMENT BELOW IS NOW MOOT BUT DELIBERATELY KEPT: it is the reason this file could sit on the OTHER runtime for two whole phases without corrupting anything, and it is the reasoning any future split must re-satisfy. setjmp/longjmp carry ZERO CRT-owned state. They read and write only the caller's own `jmp_buf` — a plain register snapshot in memory the PROGRAM allocates — and touch no heap block, no FILE*, no fd table and no errno slot, so there is no object of runtime-owned identity to exchange across the two CRTs. (`longjmp` IS dual-exported, but is bound here for consistency with the `_setjmp` that filled the buffer it consumes.) THE MEMBERSHIP RULE the co-state group applies (see tests/ffi/test_pe_crt_costate_binding.cpp) is 'does the surface accept or return a value carrying runtime-owned IDENTITY' — and by that rule this file is out, exactly as time.json is out for its plain-POD `struct tm`. | C11/C23 <setjmp.h> (7.13) — FC17.9(c) (D-CSUBSET-SETJMP). Non-local jump via a libc FFI (Option A — the synthesized alternative is REFUTED: DSS's IndirectBr needs a closed same-function target list, so it can't jump into an arbitrary ancestor frame; there is no inline asm yet). setjmp/longjmp are REAL libc exports (glibc libc.so.6, macOS libSystem, Windows ucrtbase) — this descriptor binds them exactly like the pthread/threads typedef+macro precedents. THREE realizations per format: elf+macho ship the plain 1-arg `setjmp(jmp_buf)->i32`; pe ships MSVC's 2-arg `_setjmp(env, frame)->i32` (the ucrtbase export `__intrinsic_setjmp`, reached through this row's `linkName`) PLUS a pe-only function-like MACRO `setjmp(env) -> _setjmp(env, 0)` (the stdbit.json per-format macro precedent) — frame=0 selects the plain non-SEH restore, which is correct for c-subset (no __try/setjmp interaction; the SEH-aware frame!=0 unwind is DEFERRED — D-WIN64-SEH-SCOPE). `longjmp(env, v)->void` is one entry on ALL formats (same ABI) carrying `noreturn:true` (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN — the direct call is HIR-discharged into Block{ExprStmt(call), Unreachable}). setjmp/_setjmp carry `returnsTwice:true` (D-CSUBSET-SETJMP) — a SECOND value channel mirroring noreturn: the descriptor bit → SymbolRecord.returnsTwice → a per-Call MirInstFlags::ReturnsTwice carrier at HIR->MIR (noreturn is HIR-discharged and never reaches MIR, so the flag is what the OPTIMIZER's mem2reg/inliner passes read — the walking-skeleton lands the carrier; the optimizer hardening is a follow-on). ★ jmp_buf is an OPAQUE per-ARCH-sized buffer (the program only allocates one + passes &env; libc writes its own bytes). Sizes DIFFER BY ARCH within a format, so the typedef `variants` key on BOTH {arch,format} (matchVariantWhen allowArch=true — the sys/stat.json per-arch precedent) and ENUMERATE EVERY built (arch,format) pair; a 0-match ⇒ jmp_buf is NOT injected ⇒ a later use fails loud (undefined type), never a silent wrong size. VERIFIED sizes: elf x86_64 = 200B (glibc __jmp_buf 8 longs + __mask_was_saved + 128B sigset) = arr<i64,25>; elf arm64 = 312B (22-doubleword __jmp_buf + 128B sigset) = arr<i64,39>; pe x86_64 = 256B, ALIGN 16 (MSVC _JUMP_BUFFER = SETJMP_FLOAT128 Part[16], each a 16B/16-aligned unit — _setjmp saves Xmm6-Xmm15 with `movaps`, so the buffer MUST be 16-aligned or it #GP-crashes) — expressed as arr<u128 "unsigned __int128",16>: a 16-BYTE/16-ALIGNED element (u128 aligns to the x86_64 target's maxAlignment=16) yields 256B at 16-align WITHOUT an alignas field (the alloca honors the type's natural alignment via computeLayout — pure config data, no code branch). ★★ THE `"unsigned __int128"` VOCABULARY TAG IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATION (D-CSUBSET-UINT128-TYPE, TF-C94). Once c-subset.lang.json spells `unsigned __int128` as a typeSpecifiers row NAMED `unsigned __int128`, a SOURCE-level `unsigned __int128` interns `primitive(U128, "unsigned __int128")` while an UNTAGGED `u128` here interns `primitive(U128, {})` — and type_lattice.cpp:151-163 short-circuits the empty name to the `TypeNameId{}` sentinel, so those are TWO DIFFERENT TypeIds for ONE C type. That is precisely the `ssize_t` PHANTOM recorded in shippedLibs/sys/types.json (`_Generic` matched NEITHER arm; `long long *p = aSsizeTPtr;` failed S0003), and `checkShippedTypeConsistency` does NOT catch it. MEASURED at TF-C94 before the tag, target x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec: both `unsigned __int128 *p = &env[0];` and a pointer-valued `_Generic(env[0], unsigned __int128: ..., default: ...)` failed S0003; WITH the tag both compile clean. The alternative — authoring the lang rows NAMELESS — was REJECTED: a nameless row forfeits the loader's cross-row consistency check (grammar_schema_json.cpp ~7569, gated on a non-empty name), which is what stops two spellings of one name from claiming different representations. Syntax precedent: fcntl.json:20 (`i64 \"long\"`). macho arm64 = 192B researched (_JBLEN=(14+8+2)*2=48 ints × 4B; plain jmp_buf, no sigset — we ship setjmp not sigsetjmp), over-sized to 224B = arr<i64,28> for margin on the CI-only leg (can't run locally on win/wsl/qemu — validated on the macos-arm64 CI leg). sigsetjmp/siglongjmp + the sigmask channel are DEFERRED (D-CSUBSET-SETJMP-SIGMASK). Gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,pe,macho].
